{{1967 Iowa Conference football standings}}
The '''1967 Central Dutch football team''' was an [[American football]] team that represented [[Central College (Iowa)|Central College]] of [[Pella, Iowa]], as a member of the [[American Rivers Conference|Iowa Conference]] during the [[1967 NAIA football season]]. In their fourth season under head coach [[Ron Schipper]], the Dutch compiled an 9–0 record (7–0 against conference opponents), won the Iowa Conference championship, and outscored opponents by a total of 242 to 54.<ref>{{cite web|title=1967 Football Schedule|publisher=Central College|accessdate=February 23, 2024|url=https://athletics.central.edu/sports/football/schedule/1967}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=2021 Central College Media Guide|publisher=Central College|year=2021|accessdate=February 23, 2024|url=https://athletics.central.edu/documents/2021/8/27//2021_Football_Media_Guide.pdf?id=2908}}</ref> It was Central's second consecutive undefeated regular season, though the 1966 team lost to Wisconsin-Whitewater in the NAIA playoffs.<ref>{{cite news|title=Central Football Success: Positive Attitude|newspaper=Des Moines Tribne|date=November  15, 1967|page=55|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/des-moines-tribune-central-football-succ/141951501/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>

Senior tailback Doug van Boven set school records (later surpassed) with (i) 263 rushing yards in 25 carries (10.5 average) in a game against North Central, and (ii) 1,422 rushing yards for the season.<ref> 2021 Media Guide, p. 43.</ref> Van Boven had not played organized football before enrolling at Central;<ref>{{cite news|title=Central Key: 'Moving Van'|newspaper=Des Moines Tribune|author=Jim Moackler|date=September 21, 1967|page=26|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/des-moines-tribune-central-key-moving/142004896/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Never Played Prep Football, Van Boven Is Central Star|newspaper=Times-Democrat|date=October 3, 1967|page=8|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/quad-city-times-never-played-prep-footba/142005242/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> he joined the Central football team was a [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-on]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Van Boven Walked On Now Runs Away from Central Foes|newspaper=Waterloo daily Courier|date=October 3, 1967|page=14|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-courier-van-boven-walked-on-now-runs/142005695/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> His 1,422 rushing yards led the NAIA, and his 102 points scored (on 17 toouchdowns) ranked seventh nationally.<ref>{{cite news|title=Van Boven Top Rusher|newspaper=Estherville Daily News|date=December 23, 1967|page=6|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/estherville-daily-news-van-boven-top-rus/142006882/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> At the end of the 1967 season, he was selected as the team's most valuable player and received second-team honors on the [[1967 Little All-America college football team]].<ref>2021 Media Guide, pp. 65, 85.</ref>

Seven Central players won all-conference honors: Van Boven; offensive linemen Ken Piazza and Gary Van Hulzen; defensive lineman Larry Embling; and defensive backs Gary Auxier, Nick Cookas, and Rich Vets.<ref> 2021 Media Guide, p. 61.</ref>

The team played its home games at in [[Pella, Iowa]].
